caveat: cross-strain vst meanexp = natural inter-individual expression variation (the correct data type); gene->channel aggregation hand-curated; model Hessian from 6 coarse behavioural observables.
VERDICT: DEFINITIVE NULL with the correct data type. Across 208 wild C. elegans strains (CaeNDR/Bell&Paaby cross-individual natural variation, all 14 channel genes present), natural expression covariance does NOT concentrate in the model sloppy subspace: Spearman rho=+0.21 (if anything the WRONG direction), sloppy/stiff variance ratio 1.14x with permutation p=0.997 (random gene arrangements give a HIGHER ratio). Combined with the CeNGEN cross-cell-type null, the prediction 'real biological variation concentrates along the behavioural sloppy eigenvectors' is NOT supported. Likely because conductance-scaling parameters do not map linearly to mRNA expression levels, and expression covariance is shaped by co-regulation unrelated to behavioural sloppiness. The core results (behaviour low-dim, complementary tiling, biophysical interpretability, cross-species) do not depend on this interpretation.
